analysis:
The only change in this PR is test-only: lines 683-687 of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Service/ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift. It adds assertions to failedCommitPreservesMatchingHashAndFingerprint. After a failed or unconfirmed model-switch commit, `loop.autopilotBusyReasons()` must not contain `.modelSwitch`. It must contain `.draining` only when the connection dropped. The existing assertion that `state.refusingNewWork == dropConnection` stays. No production code, endpoint, key handling, attestation, or authorization logic changed, and there is no new attack surface.

Security relevance: the new assertions pin fail-closed admission. When a commit's coordinator confirmation is unconfirmed (dropped connection), the provider keeps refusing new work and keeps the new hash/snapshot. When the commit is rejected, the provider rolls back to the old selection and reopens admission. This is consistent with TB-002 and TB-011 expectations that a stale or unconfirmed capacity or advertised-model state does not receive private work. It also fits the weight-hash binding concerns in T-012 and T-027. The tests use mocks, with no secrets and no real network. Temporary roots are removed in `defer`.

Remaining question: `autopilotBusyReasons()` and the `.modelSwitch` and `.draining` semantics are defined in unchanged production code that was not supplied, so I could not verify the production behavior the new assertions encode. This is a test-coverage observation, not a regression.
